entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighty and censorious - it treats the behaviour as a failure of judgement grave enough to be named, where *craziness* simply calls it mad.
examples: Follies and nonsense, whims and inconsistencies, do divert me, I own, and I laugh at them whenever I can.
to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others

entries.definition: acting like a clown or buffoon
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Aimed at clowning and buffoonery - antic performance rather than the misjudgement *folly* names, so the disapproval comes with amusement in it.

entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The softest way of naming senseless behaviour here, framing it as something permitted or allowed oneself rather than something to be condemned.

entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest word in the set - it does not call the behaviour unwise but insane, and means the charge to land.

entries.definition: the act of moving with great haste
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Great speed as a sudden break away, all abruptness and no blame - the carelessness that shadows *hurry* is absent.

entries.definition: the act of moving with great haste
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Speed as a short spirited burst, brisk and deliberate beside the startled suddenness of *bolt*.
examples: he made a dash for the door

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and weighty, naming the hurry as a fault to be answered for where *hurry* merely reports it.
examples: in his haste to leave he forgot his book
Well, Jane, make haste and tell us; make haste, my love.
In his haste he knocked the cup off the table.

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest name for going fast and going badly at once, with the carelessness carried quietly rather than pressed.
examples: could serve only to amuse her in the hurry and confusion of the following hour

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on momentum - a harder-edged, more headlong version of *hurry*, where the speed is what overrides the care.

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The participle keeps the careless speed running on as an activity rather than a single lapse, unlike the finished act *rush* names.

entries.definition: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the hurry small and skittering, so the loss of dignity comes out as comic rather than damning.

entries.definition: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The undignified hurry as graceless floundering - effortful disorder where *scamper* is merely quick and silly.

entries.definition: steadfast in purpose or devotion or affection
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Straightforward praise for not wavering, and it covers purpose, devotion and affection alike rather than loyalty alone.
examples: a man constant in adherence to his ideals
a constant lover
constant as the northern star
She was constant in her affection for him through every trouble.

entries.definition: constant and unchanging
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Absolute and cool: it reports that a thing does not change rather than crediting it with holding fast, so no praise attaches the way it does to *steadfast*.
examples: the immutable laws of nature

entries.definition: firm and dependable especially in loyalty
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Weightier than *constant* because it adds dependability, making the firmness something others can lean on.
examples: a steadfast ally

entries.definition: tireless
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of what never runs out, measuring steadiness by supply rather than by the refusal to vary that *constant* asks for.
examples: unfailing loyalty
unfailing good spirits

entries.definition: tireless
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same tirelessness as *unfailing*, but figured as a pace that never slackens rather than a store that never empties.
examples: unflagging courtesy

entries.definition: instill (into a person) by constant repetition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and wearing - the thing goes in by sheer relentless repetition, with none of the instruction *inculcate* implies.
examples: he dinned the lessons into his students
His father dinned the same warning into him every single night.

entries.definition: teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and deliberate - repetition put to the work of teaching, and admonition counts as much as drilling.
examples: inculcate values into the young generation

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most offhand of these, conceding that the expectation rests on little where *reckon* sounds decided.
examples: I guess she is angry at me for standing her up

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Reaches the belief by picturing how things must be, so it sounds more speculative than *think* even when it means the same.
examples: I imagine she earned a lot of money with her new novel
the sort of cautiousness to which you, I imagine, have been alluding
don't imagine it was from any silly cause

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal, and it frames the belief as an opinion delivered rather than a thought privately held as with *think*.

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and flatly settled — states the expectation as arrived at, with none of the tentativeness of *suppose*.

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Holds the belief provisionally, as something granted rather than asserted outright the way *think* asserts it.
examples: "Do you suppose them to be in London?"
There are few people in England, I suppose, who have more true enjoyment of music than myself

entries.definition: hold in suspicion; believe to be guilty
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Belief pointed at a person and against them — where *think* merely holds a view, this one holds someone guilty.
examples: The police suspected him of the theft, but they could prove nothing.

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain, unmarked way to hold something to be so, without the hedge of *suppose* or the formality of *opine*.
examples: I thought to find her in a bad state
he didn't think to find her in the kitchen
I thought he would arrive before dinner.

entries.definition: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval at its floor: it grants only that the manner was not rude, the minimal end of what *polite* also lets stretch to a satisfactory observance.
examples: even if he didn't like them he should have been civil
Mr. Bingley was unaffectedly civil in his answer, and forced his younger sister to be civil also
It was more than civil; it was really attentive

entries.definition: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits the social usages as kept rather than merely the offence as avoided, though the consideration it reports stays sufficient and unremarkable rather than warm.
